mumu_adb_description: Maa native Android capture and touch. Requires Limbus already in the foreground; does not launch the game.
description: Native Windows Limbus automation with MaaFramework
windows_window_description: MaaEnd-style background capture, cursor-position window mouse messages and PostMessage keys. Verify the expected next page after input.
windows_background_description: Window-position mouse messages and PostMessage keys. Test whether this game accepts background input.
windows_front_description: Screen capture and foreground mouse/keyboard input. Keep the game visible.
global_build_description: How this team is used in the Mirror Dungeon: which gifts it goes for, who deploys first, which starlight buffs it takes. It corresponds to TEAMS # in the game. All three default to "unchanged"; a change is checked and saved before the next Mirror task starts, and the team of a run in progress can only be changed after that run ends.
mirror_team_systems_description: Which systems' E.G.O gifts this team goes for in the Mirror Dungeon: the shop, floor gifts and the starting gift all follow it.
mirror_team_keywords_description: The same ten keywords, in the same order, as the shop's Keyword Refresh in the game: seven systems, then three damage types. Tick one or several; none ticked means no restriction and the program chooses by score. Keywordless, at the end, also buys gifts that work for any team.
mirror_team_order_description: Who deploys first. The input of "Write the whole order" can be typed, or filled in by the task "Read the teams' deployment orders": it reads the order on the game's team screen and writes it here, where you see it afterwards and can change it. "Follow the game" uses whatever the game shows every time and only records it.
mirror_team_order_game: Follow the order set in the game
mirror_team_order_text_description: Write the sinners in deployment order by number or name, separated by spaces, for example 6 8 7 3 5; the ones you do not name follow in roster order. Numbers: 1 Yi Sang, 2 Faust, 3 Don Quixote, 4 Ryoshu, 5 Meursault, 6 Hong Lu, 7 Heathcliff, 8 Ishmael, 9 Rodion, 10 Sinclair, 11 Outis, 12 Gregor.
main_open_game_description: Launch Android through Maa and verify the foreground; leave an already open game running; when the game does not come to the front, close it and start it once more. Connect the game window first on Windows.
main_mirror_description: Use global saved builds and deployment order. Choose one team or a rotation here. Hard by default; spending requires a configured budget.
main_experience_description: Uses a saved team and navigates through Drive to Luxcavation. An unfinished Mirror run blocks navigation. Stage selection, farming and cost verification are not yet supported.
main_thread_description: Uses a saved team and navigates through Drive to Luxcavation. An unfinished Mirror run blocks navigation. Stage selection, farming and cost verification are not yet supported.
main_rewards_description: Claim rewards for the current cleared Mirror run with its module budget. Mail and daily mission collection are not yet supported.
mirror_star_team: Follow the current team (set under the team in global settings)
mirror_star_description: The game does not remember the last run's graces; they are chosen again every run. So a plan comes from one of two places: the team's own (set under the team in the global settings) or this task's. With "Follow the current team", a team that has no plan uses this task's.
mirror_initial_keyword_description: Selects the initial gift group. Floor gifts still use the saved build systems and preferences.
mirror_run_count_description: How many complete Mirror Dungeon runs after this one? A run counts only after five cleared floors, a claimed payout and a return to the lobby; 0 means no number named and the window walks to another bound.
mirror_shop_fusion_description: Before leaving a shop, open "Fuse Gifts" once: a recipe the game itself lists under "Fusion Available" (all gifts owned, fixed result) is fused. Only a recipe whose forecast reads 100% is fused; Wishmaking is never ticked (no Starlight is spent) and no random fusion is made. Fusing costs no coins.
mirror_defeat_accept: After a wipe with the retries used up
mirror_defeat_accept_description: When every Sinner falls in a battle the program retries first (twice at most). If the stage is wiped again after that: "End the run" picks "Accept results" on the defeat page and confirms it, which ends the run, and the settings under "Claim rewards after a clear" then apply; "Stop and wait for me" stops on the defeat page and presses nothing.
mirror_reward_claim_description: Whether the rewards are claimed and the lobby reached after five floors are cleared. A run's rewards cost 5 modules; with weekly bonuses switched on in the game it is 6 or 18. The program never changes that switch and never clicks "Give Up Rewards". When the offer cannot be read it stops on the reward page and clicks nothing.
mirror_reward_claim_off: Do not claim (stop on the reward page)
mirror_reward_claim_lost: A run that ended before the dungeon was cleared (lost)
mirror_reward_claim_lost_description: When a run ends before all five floors are cleared, its rewards are smaller but cost the same 5 modules. With "Do not claim" the program stops on the reward page and presses nothing; the game will not start another run until this one is dealt with. The program never presses "Give Up Rewards". A lost run is not claimed while weekly bonuses are switched on. A claimed lost run is not counted as a completed run and the team does not rotate.
mirror_reward_claim_lost_off: Do not claim (stop on the reward page)
mirror_schedule_description: For running on a timer: the Mirror Dungeon is played only on the chosen days, and once the day's runs are done another start ends at once without touching the game. Booked per game-server day (by default the day turns at 06:00 Korea time). "No schedule" plays on every start.
mirror_runs_per_day_description: Complete runs to finish on a chosen day. A run counts once five floors are cleared, the reward is claimed and the lobby is reached.
mirror_preferences_description: Edits add or remove only the selected preferences when the Mirror task starts. Systems, order and other entries are preserved. Active-build changes stop; blocks win.
mirror_battle_assignment_description: Choose the proven game auto-assignment button. Start submits an assigned turn. Observe stops without battle inputs; this does not edit individual skills.
mirror_battle_observe: Observe only (debug: stops at the battle)
reward_module_budget_description: Binds to the current cleared run when this task starts. Preserve the saved budget by default; claim only within the cap. Weekly bonuses, Lunacy and conversion stay unchanged.
mirror_shop_policy_description: Boss-adjacent shop visits. Keep your saved rule by default. Manual uses the refresh limit and coin reserve below as written. Learned may only obey those same two settings and the existing gift allow/block list, and falls back to the rule when there are no recorded samples; it is not a trained purchase model. This setting decides no purchase by itself.
mirror_shop_refresh_description: Plain refreshes per shop visit. Pick any number from 0 to 5, or keep your saved value (2 when nothing was ever saved). Nothing here can mean "refresh without limit".
mirror_shop_coin_reserve_description: Coins kept back and never spent in a shop visit. Pick any number from 0 to 500, or keep your saved value (500 when nothing was ever saved). What you pick is used as written, so you can lower it yourself; the learned rule only obeys it and will never lower this floor on its own. A visit that would still carry more than 1500 coins out spends the shelf on what is affordable instead, so the run reaches the floor boss with spent coins rather than a hoard.
main_detect_emulator_description: Run once while the emulator is connected: it works out which emulator the connection belongs to (MuMu instances are recognised), and keeps how to start it and its ADB address in your data folder. After that "Launch emulator" can use "the remembered emulator" with nothing typed in, and "Close emulator" knows which one to close. Read-only: no emulator setting is changed. It also reports whether the resolution, DPI and frame rate are the ones the program was verified on.
main_close_game_description: Stops Limbus Company and confirms it is no longer in front. Meant for the end of the task list; a battle in progress is not saved.
main_close_emulator_description: Asks the manager program of the emulator to close the one instance that is connected, and waits until it stops answering. Only that instance; no other is touched. Needs "Detect and remember the emulator" to have been run. For shutdown, sleep and quitting this program use "Computer action" and "End process" under "Add task → Special tasks".
launch_emulator_source_description: "The remembered emulator" starts the one saved by the task "Detect and remember the emulator", with nothing to fill in; if none has been remembered the pretask fails and says so. "Manual entry" uses the four settings below.
launch_emulator_description: Before the device is connected, start the emulator and wait until its ADB address answers. An emulator that is already running is left alone. Leave the program empty to open the emulator yourself. The Open game task then starts the game itself.
launch_emulator_program: Full path of the emulator program
launch_emulator_arguments: Arguments (for example, which instance to start)
main_read_team_order_description: Open the team screen outside a dungeon first (the TEAMS list on the left, twelve Identity cards with their deployment numbers on the right), then run this. Starting at TEAMS #1 it selects the teams down the list one by one, reads the numbers on each team's twelve cards and writes them straight into that team's "Deployment order" in the global settings: the choice becomes "Write the whole order" and the input holds what was read, as sinner numbers in deployment order (1 Yi Sang, 2 Faust, 3 Don Quixote, 4 Ryoshu, 5 Meursault, 6 Hong Lu, 7 Heathcliff, 8 Ishmael, 9 Rodion, 10 Sinclair, 11 Outis, 12 Gregor). A run already in progress keeps its order; the other teams deploy the new order from their next entry. You can then see it there, edit it or choose something else. It presses only rows of the list and drags the list when needed; no card is pressed. A team that cannot be read completely is skipped with the reason.
mirror_team_stars_description: Which graces this team takes into the Mirror Dungeon, at which level, and whether the owned stock may be used. Applied when the Mirror task's "Whose starlight plan" is "Follow the current team" (the default).
read_team_count: How many teams to read (from TEAMS #1 down)
read_team_count_description: The first teams from the top. 3 reads TEAMS #1, #2 and #3.
mirror_star_plan_description: The three "all" choices are the game's "Select All Graces" plus "Enhance All". With "Tick my own" there is one row per level: tick a card in the row of the level you want; a card ticked in two rows takes the higher. The numbers are the costs at the three levels (plain / + / ++).
mirror_star_row_description: One tick takes the card at this level.
mirror_star_spend_description: Each run has an allowance of starlight (Available, top right of the page); what is left goes to the clear rewards unless the page's "Convert Starlight to Cost" is ticked (this program does not tick it). When a plan costs more than the allowance the game takes the rest from your owned stock. By default the stock is not touched: cards are bought in order as far as the allowance goes.
mirror_star_spend_allowance: The run's allowance only; leave the stock alone
mirror_star_spend_stock_cap: May use the stock, up to this much a run
mirror_star_spend_stock_all: May use the stock, as much as the plan needs
mirror_star_cap: Most starlight taken from the stock per run
mirror_shop_refresh_paid_description: "Free refreshes only": the shop is refreshed only while the refresh button prints a price of 0 (free refreshes come from graces such as Star of the Beginning and Moon Star-shop); a refresh that costs coins is never pressed. The refresh limit above still applies.
mirror_shop_skill_mode_description: The shelf's "Replace … Skill": swap one lower skill of an opening frontline Identity for a tier 3 skill, for coins. Only for Identities that were deployed at the start, at most once per sinner per shop visit, only above the coin reserve, and the cheapest option. The program selects the card, checks on the next frame that nothing changed, presses Confirm, and checks the coin difference and the skill counts; if Confirm changed nothing it cancels and never presses it again.
mirror_shop_skill_keep_one_each: Buy, keeping at least one tier 1 and one tier 2 skill
mirror_shop_skill_keep_one_s2: Buy, keeping at least one tier 2 skill
